sections.title: Molecular profile of ovarian clear cell carcinoma
sections.intro: OCCC is a **SWI/SNF (ARID1A) and PI3K-pathway–driven, TP53-wild-type, homologous-recombination-proficient** carcinoma arising in a background of endometriosis. None of the biomarkers that select first-line maintenance or platinum-resistant therapy in HGSC (BRCA/HRD, FRα) is common here, and no targeted agent against the defining alterations has been active in a clinical trial (Table 3C).

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.md:
1. **MMR IHC is worth doing** — about 6% of OCCC are MMR-deficient, they present young, and roughly half of IHC-MMRd ovarian cancers carry a germline variant across histotypes [9,10]. It flags Lynch evaluation and a checkpoint-inhibitor candidate.
2. **HRD testing is low yield** (HRD 2.3% of 44 [7]). First-line PARPi maintenance trials excluded clear cell unless germline BRCA-mutated (Table 2B).
3. **HER2 IHC 2+ is the common result (45–63%); 3+ is 6–9%** [15,16]. Scoring system matters: the MD Anderson series used breast criteria. No clear-cell–specific T-DXd data exist.
4. **PD-L1 CPS did not predict response** in the clear-cell combination trials: LARA responses occurred although 85% were CPS 0 [5]. KEYNOTE-B96's CPS ≥1 selection was generated in an 86% HGSC population [14].
5. **FRα-high is uncommon (~10%) and untested in this histotype** [1,19].

notes.title: No randomized adjuvant evidence specific to clear cell
notes.md:
- Clear cell was 14–31% of the early-stage RCTs, because GOG-157, GOG-175, ACTION and ICON7 made stage I clear cell eligible **by histology alone**. That was a design decision, not a finding. The clear cell subgroup HRs are 0.90 (6 vs 3 cycles) and 0.981 (maintenance paclitaxel), both with CIs spanning 0.4–3 [27,28]. The ICON1/ACTION clear cell death counts (16/68 vs 17/62) do not show the pooled benefit [23].
- ACTION's benefit was confined to incompletely staged patients [25]. Most observational OCCC series now include staged patients, and the Bogani meta-analysis found no DFS/OS effect in stage I overall and an OS association only in stage IC [30]. It is uncontrolled and confounded by indication.
- **Bevacizumab is not supported** in high-risk early-stage disease (ICON7 subgroup OS HR 1.49) [29].
- JGOG3017's stage I strata compare two regimens with 2-year PFS of ~89% in both arms [8]; they say nothing about observation.

notes.title: Three traps in Table 2A
notes.md:
1. **Carboplatin–paclitaxel is the first-line standard because JGOG3017 was negative, not because it was shown to work well in OCCC.** Irinotecan–cisplatin was not superior, and stage II–IV 2-year PFS was only 42.6–52.5% [8]. Adding temsirolimus did not beat historical controls [31].
2. **Schedule and route changes that helped HGSC did not help clear cell.** Dose-dense paclitaxel: clear cell/mucinous PFS HR 1.03 [32]. IP carboplatin: clear cell PFS HR 0.96 [34]. Both are small, exploratory subgroups.
3. **Bevacizumab has no clear cell OS signal** (ICON7 clear cell OS HR 1.09, n=159) [29]. In GOG-0218 clear cell was 2.9% and not reported separately [37].

notes.title: There is no first-line maintenance evidence in clear cell carcinoma
notes.md: SOLO1 and PRIMA excluded clear cell; PAOLA-1 admitted it only with a germline BRCA mutation (2 patients) [38,18,39]. Where clear cell was eligible (ATHENA-MONO, DUO-O, KEYLYNK-001) it was 3–6% and not reported [40–42]. With HRD in 2.3% of OCCC [7], the HRD-driven maintenance logic of OVCA_HGSC_Algorithm_v1.2 Table 2B does not transfer. The only clear cell maintenance-era subgroup is IMagyn050 (atezolizumab, PFS HR 0.64, 0.33–1.24, n=51) [43] — hypothesis-generating in a negative trial.

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: Clear cell recurrence evidence does not sort cleanly by platinum-free interval. **3A** and **3B** keep the HGSC split for all-histology trials, with each row's clear cell share. **3C** holds the clear-cell–specific trials, which enrolled after ≥1 platinum line **regardless of PFI**; their PFI mix is given in the `Prior systemic therapy` cell.

notes.title: Why this split exists
notes.md:
1. **Platinum sensitivity is prognostic in OCCC too.** In JGOG3017's 166 recurrences, median post-progression survival was 18.8 months if platinum-sensitive vs 10.9 months if resistant (HR 1.88) [44]. Pooling both, as the 3C trials do, blurs that.
2. **The 3C trials differ in line of therapy**: MoST-CIRCUIT allowed 0–1 prior lines (32% treatment-naive) [4]; PEACOCC had a median 3 prior lines [11]; DART up to 8 [20]. Their ORRs are not comparable to each other or to a platinum-resistant 3B trial.

notes.title: Reading notes for Table 3
notes.md:
- **Chemotherapy in recurrent OCCC is weak even as a control arm**: MOCCA's physician's-choice chemotherapy gave ORR 18.8% and median PFS 14 weeks [13].
- **Single-agent targeted drugs aimed at the biology have failed**: sunitinib ORR 6.7% [21], cabozantinib 0% [59], dasatinib 3.6% (ARID1A-selected) [22], ENMD-2076 3 PR of 38 [60].
- **PD-(L)1 monotherapy is modest and did not beat chemotherapy.** MOCCA durvalumab ORR 9.7%, PFS HR 1.6 [13]; PEACOCC 25% (85% ovarian) [11]; KEYNOTE-100 clear cell 15.8% (n=19) [54]; NINJA clear cell OS HR 0.78, CI crossing 1 [52].
- **Combinations gave the highest ORRs, all single-arm**: PD-1 + VEGF — INOVA 40.5% [58], LARA 40% (89% ovarian) [5]; nivolumab + ipilimumab — MoST-CIRCUIT ovarian 55% [4] but **DART ovarian 15.8%** [20]. The same drugs differed by ipilimumab schedule (q3w induction vs q6w continuous), line of therapy (0–1 vs median 2) and toxicity (one fatal myocarditis in MoST-CIRCUIT). No combination has been tested against chemotherapy.
- **Count by site.** Ovarian primaries were 24/27 (LARA), 41/48 (PEACOCC), 24/28 (MoST-CIRCUIT) and 19/32 (DART). DART's endometrial and cervical patients had no RECIST responses [20]. Endometrial results are in EMCA_ClearCell_Algorithm_v1.2.
- **PARPi maintenance, mirvetuximab and relacorilant have no clear cell data** (❌ rows). KEYNOTE-B96 admitted clear cell (8%) but did not report it separately [14].
- Not tabulated: **BrUOG 354** (nivolumab ± ipilimumab) and **NICCC / ENGOT-ov36** (nintedanib vs chemotherapy) are cited in the Blanc-Durand review [1] but no PubMed-indexed publication was found (2026-09-15).
